topic_theme: Kelp DAO Exploit and DeFi United Recovery Effort
primary_headline: DeFi United Raises Funds to Cover $292 Million Kelp DAO Exploit Aftermath
combined_key_facts: A ~$292 million security breach involving a KelpDAO integration vulnerability with LayerZero led to massive bad debt on Aave.
Aave experienced a significant drop in Total Value Locked (TVL), between $10 billion and $12 billion, as users rushed to withdraw funds.
A recovery initiative named 'DeFi United' was launched by Aave and other protocols to stabilize the rsETH token and recapitalize the ~$200 million in bad debt.
According to Arkham, the effort has raised ~$160 million, with major contributions from Mantle and the Aave DAO.
Aave founder Stani Kulechov personally contributed 5,000 ETH.
Aave Labs has formally proposed that the Arbitrum DAO unfreeze 30,765 ETH (worth ~$73.5 million) tied to the exploiter's wallet and direct the funds to the DeFi United recovery address.
An additional $215 million has been pledged by entities like Arbitrum, Mantle, Ether.fi, and Lido, which are pending governance votes.
aggregated_raw_content: Lending platform Aave has raised about $160 million it needs to cover the $200 million in bad debt left behind by the year's largest decentralized finance (DeFi) exploit, Arkham posted on X on Saturday. Last week, Aave and several major crypto firms announced a coordinated recovery effort to stabilize DeFi markets after a $292 million security breach left the crypto borrowing sector's largest lender facing a financial crisis. Called DeFi United and led by Aave service providers, the effort’s goal is to restore support for rsETH, the yield-bearing derivative token of ether (ETH) at the core of the exploit. The exploit is traced back to a KelpDAO integration vulnerability with LayerZero, where an attacker minted 116,500 unbacked rsETH tokens. That left Aave with impaired collateral, triggering a run on deposits as lenders rushed to exit, ultimately withdrawing $10 billion. Aave Labs has proposed that the decentralized autonomous organization behind Arbitrum unfreeze $73.5 million in Ether tied to the Kelp DAO attack and to direct those funds to ‘DeFi United,’ a fund aimed at restoring rsETH and compensating its holders. Last week, the Arbitrum Security Council moved to freeze 30,765 Ether (ETH) held in a wallet connected to the $293 million Kelp exploit. The submission was made with the support of Kelp DAO, LayerZero, Ether.fi and Compound, four of the several crypto protocols affected by the hack. Dune Analytics data shows that about $21 million in contributions has already been made, with contributions including those from Aave Labs CEO Stani Kulechov, Aave Labs head of contracts Emilio Frangella, Kelp DAO, and others. Another $215 million has been pledged by Arbitrum, Mantle, Ether.fi and Lido to assist the recovery effort, which are subject to governance votes. Aave was hit hard by the Kelp DAO exploit, with its total value locked falling nearly $12 billion in a week, leaving more than $190 million in bad debt.
